This appeal is preferred against the judgement and award dated 16th February, 2018 passed by the learned Additional District Judge-cum-Judge, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, 5th Court, Paschim Medinipur in M.A.C. Case No.164 of 2013 granting compensation of Rs.1,25,000/- together with interest in favour of the claimant-injured under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

entities.text: District Judge-cum-Judge, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, 5th Court, Paschim Medinipur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The brief fact of the case is that on 9th May, 2010 while the victim was proceeding towards Chinchira in offending vehicle bearing registration No.WB-33/7841 for reaching her relative's house and when the offending vehicle reached near Feko More it capsized due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Due to the aforesaid reason the victim sustained grievous bleeding injuries on her person and she was treated at Jhargram S.D. Hospital from 9.5.2010 to 21.5.2010.
In relation to the injuries, the victim filed application for compensation of Rs.3,00,000/- together with interest under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
In order to establish her case, the claimant-injured examined herself and another two witnesses and also produced documents which have been marked as exhibits 1 to 16, respectively.
The appellant-Insurance Company did not adduce any evidence.

Upon considering the materials on record and having heard the learned Advocates for the respective parties, the learned Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.1,25,000/- together with interest in favour of the claimant-injured under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgement and award, the Insurance Company has preferred the present appeal.

sentences.text: Mr. Deb Narayan Ray, learned Advocate for the appellant-Insurance Company submits that the victim did not sustain any injury in the said accident and therefore, the compensation awarded by the learned Tribunal is liable to be set aside.

In reply to the contentions raised on behalf of the appellant-Insurance Company, Mr. Narendra Nath Maity, learned Advocate for the respondent-claimant submits that the claimant-injured soon after accident was admitted to Jhargram S.D. Hospital on 9.5.2010 and she was discharged on 21.5.2010 which is evident from the materials and documents produced by the claimant and therefore, the award passed in favour of the claimant-injured does not call for interference.

Since the respondent no.2, owner of the offending vehicle, did not contest the claim application before the learned Tribunal, hence service of notice of appeal upon the said respondent is dispensed with.
Having heard the learned Advocate for the respective parties, it appears that the present appeal hinges on a salutary issue as to whether the claimant-injured sustained injury in the said accident or not.
In order to appreciate the aforesaid issue it would be apposite to refer to the evidence adduced by the claimant.

P.W.1, injured-claimant deposed that on 9.5.2010 while she was proceeding towards Chinchira on the offending vehicle, it capsized at Feko More, due to which she sustained injuries and was treated at Jhargram S.D. Hospital as indoor patient from 9.5.2010 to 21.5.2010.
Such evidence of P.W.1 has not been rebutted in cross-examination or by any independent witness.
P.W. 3 is an eye-witness of the occurrence.
He also deposed that he witnessed the accident which took place on 9.5.2010 in which the victim and others were injured.
He also deposed that the victim was taken to hospital.
The claimant also adduced evidence of one employee of Jhargram S.D. Hospital who produced the bed-head ticket of the victim-injured.
The bed-head ticket of the claimant-injured shows that the claimant-injured was admitted to hospital on 9.5.2010 with history of road traffic accident and was discharged on 21.5.2010.

The continuation sheet of the bed- head ticket shows that the victim sustained right sub condylar fracture of mandible, displacement of vertical fracture, scalp injury for which she was treated in the hospital.

In view of the aforesaid evidence adduced on behalf of the claimant, the argument advanced by Mr.
Ray, learned Advocate for the appellant-Insurance Company does not stand to reason.
Accordingly, the award passed by the learned Tribunal in favour of the claimant-injured does not call for interference.

It is found that the appellant-Insurance Company has deposited a sum of Rs.1,70,860/- in terms of order of this Court passed on 14th June, 2018 before the registry of this Court vide O.D. Chalan No.907 dated 10.7.2018 as well as statutory deposit of Rs.25,000/- vide O.D. Chalan No.076 dated The National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Jharna Pal & Anr on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14047412/
2 18.4.2018.
The learned Registrar General of this Court is directed to disburse the aforesaid amount in favour of the claimant- injured upon satisfaction of her identity and proof of payment of ad valerom court fee,
if not already paid.
The claimant-injured is entitled to receive the amount of Rs.1,70,860/- together with accrued interest.
